### Spec 2 — Global PCA + Location as predictor

```{r sem-sens-loc-setup}
# Encode Location as a binary dummy: Nubra = 1, Tsomoriri = 0
sem_data_loc <- sem_data %>%
  mutate(Loc_bin = as.numeric(Location == "Nubra"))

cat("Location dummy: Nubra =", sum(sem_data_loc$Loc_bin),
    "| Tsomoriri =", sum(sem_data_loc$Loc_bin == 0), "\n")
```

```{r sem-sens-loc-fit, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
sem_model_loc <- '
  # Env + Location -> vegetation
  VegPC1  ~ a1*Dist_z + a2*TopoPC1 + a3*Loc_bin

  # Veg + Env + Location -> soil
  SoilPC1 ~ b*VegPC1 + c1*Dist_z + c2*TopoPC1 + c3*Loc_bin

  # Indirect effects
  ind_dist := a1 * b
  ind_topo := a2 * b
  ind_loc  := a3 * b

  # Total effects on soil
  tot_dist := a1 * b + c1
  tot_topo := a2 * b + c2
  tot_loc  := a3 * b + c3
'

sem_loc <- sem(
  sem_model_loc,
  data      = sem_data_loc,
  estimator = "ML",
  se        = "bootstrap",
  bootstrap = 1000
)

fit_loc <- fitMeasures(sem_loc, c("chisq","df","pvalue","cfi","rmsea","srmr"))
cat("Global PCA + Location SEM fit:\n"); print(round(fit_loc, 3))
cat("\nR-squared:\n"); print(lavInspect(sem_loc, "r2"))
```

```{r sem-sens-loc-tables}
loc_labels <- c(
  Dist_z  = "Distance (z)",
  TopoPC1 = "TopoPC1 (z)",

  VegPC1  = "Veg. colonisation PC1",
  SoilPC1 = "Soil development PC1"
)
ind_labels_loc <- c(
  ind_dist = "Distance -> Veg -> Soil (indirect)",
  ind_topo = "TopoPC1  -> Veg -> Soil (indirect)",
  ind_loc  = "Location -> Veg -> Soil (indirect)",
  tot_dist = "Distance -> Soil (total)",
  tot_topo = "TopoPC1  -> Soil (total)",
  tot_loc  = "Location -> Soil (total)"
)

param_loc <- fmt_params(sem_loc)

direct_loc <- param_loc %>%
  filter(Type == "Direct") %>%
  mutate(
    Response  = dplyr::recode(rhs, !!!loc_labels),
    Predictor = dplyr::recode(lhs, !!!loc_labels)
  ) %>%
  select(Response, Predictor, `Beta (std)` = std_beta, SE,
         `95% CI lo` = CI_lo, `95% CI hi` = CI_hi, p = p_val, ` ` = Sig)

nv_l <- sum(direct_loc$Response == loc_labels["VegPC1"])
ns_l <- sum(direct_loc$Response == loc_labels["SoilPC1"])

direct_loc %>%
  kable(caption = paste0(
    "Spec 2 (global PCA + Location) — direct paths. ",
    "Global PCA scores; Location (Nubra=1, Tsomoriri=0) as an exogenous dummy."
  )) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped","hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  pack_rows("-> Veg. colonisation PC1", 1,         nv_l) %>%
  pack_rows("-> Soil development PC1",  nv_l + 1,  nv_l + ns_l)

param_loc %>%
  filter(Type == "Indirect/Total") %>%
  mutate(Effect = dplyr::recode(lhs, !!!ind_labels_loc)) %>%
  select(Effect, `Beta (std)` = std_beta, SE,
         `95% CI lo` = CI_lo, `95% CI hi` = CI_hi, p = p_val, ` ` = Sig) %>%
  kable(caption = "Spec 2 (global PCA + Location) — indirect and total effects") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped","hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  pack_rows("Indirect (env/loc -> veg -> soil)", 1, 3) %>%
  pack_rows("Total (direct + indirect)",         4, 6)
```

```{r export-sem-figures, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
export_sem_figure <- function(name, fig) {
  png_file <- file.path(sem_fig_dir, paste0(name, "_REVISION.png"))
  svg_file <- file.path(sem_fig_dir, paste0(name, "_REVISION.svg"))

  ggsave(
    filename = png_file,
    plot = fig$plot,
    width = fig$width,
    height = fig$height,
    dpi = 300,
    bg = "white"
  )

  save_gg_svg(
    filename = svg_file,
    plot = fig$plot,
    width = fig$width,
    height = fig$height
  )

  tibble(figure = name, png = png_file, svg = svg_file)
}
```

## Results text

```{r results-helpers, include=FALSE}
# ── Inline-code helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Extract a standardised path coefficient from a lavaan fit
std_beta <- function(fit, lhs_v, rhs_v)
  round(parameterEstimates(fit, standardized = TRUE) %>%
          filter(lhs == lhs_v, rhs == rhs_v, op == "~") %>%
          pull(std.all), 2)

# Extract a p-value
pval <- function(fit, lhs_v, rhs_v) {
  p <- parameterEstimates(fit, standardized = TRUE) %>%
    filter(lhs == lhs_v, rhs == rhs_v, op == "~") %>%
    pull(pvalue)
  if (p < 0.001) "< 0.001" else paste0("= ", round(p, 3))
}

# Extract a defined (indirect/total) effect
def_est <- function(fit, label_v)
  round(parameterEstimates(fit, standardized = TRUE) %>%
          filter(lhs == label_v, op == ":=") %>%
          pull(std.all), 2)

def_p <- function(fit, label_v) {
  p <- parameterEstimates(fit, standardized = TRUE) %>%
    filter(lhs == label_v, op == ":=") %>%
    pull(pvalue)
  if (p < 0.001) "< 0.001" else paste0("= ", round(p, 3))
}

# R-squared for a node
r2 <- function(fit, node)
  round(unname(lavInspect(fit, "r2")[node]), 2)

# Fit index — NA-safe (just-identified models return NA for pvalue/chisq)
fi <- function(fit, index) {
  val <- suppressWarnings(unname(fitMeasures(fit, index)))
  if (length(val) == 0 || is.na(val)) return(NA_real_)
  round(val, 3)
}

# Display chi-square test safely
chisq_str <- function(fit) {
  p <- fi(fit, "pvalue")
  df_val <- fi(fit, "df")
  chisq_val <- fi(fit, "chisq")
  p_str <- if (is.na(p)) "n/a (saturated model, df = 0)" else
    if (p < 0.001) "< 0.001" else paste0("= ", p)
  paste0("chisq = ", chisq_val, ", df = ", df_val, ", p ", p_str)
}

# Fit quality label based on CFI/RMSEA (robust to NA pvalue)
fit_quality <- function(fit) {
  df_val <- fi(fit, "df")
  if (!is.na(df_val) && df_val == 0) {
    return("saturated")
  }
  cfi   <- fi(fit, "cfi")
  rmsea <- fi(fit, "rmsea")
  p     <- fi(fit, "pvalue")
  ok_p  <- is.na(p) || p >= 0.05
  ok_cfi   <- !is.na(cfi)   && cfi   >= 0.95
  ok_rmsea <- !is.na(rmsea) && rmsea <= 0.08
  if (ok_p && ok_cfi && ok_rmsea) "good"
  else if (ok_p || (ok_cfi && ok_rmsea)) "acceptable"
  else "marginal"
}

# PCA % variance for PC1
pct_var <- function(pca_obj)
  round(summary(pca_obj)$importance[2, 1] * 100, 1)

# Median rarefied diversity
med_div <- function(col) round(median(col, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
```

### SEM results

#### Composite axes

The first principal component of cover variables explained
`r pct_var(pca_cover)`% of total cover variance (VegPC1), with
positive loadings on lichen and moss cover and negative loadings on bare soil
and stone cover, representing a gradient from bare, recently-deglaciated
substrate to vegetated surfaces.
The soil development axis (SoilPC1) captured `r pct_var(pca_soil)`% of soil
variance, with positive loadings on organic matter, nitrogen, and phosphorus.
The topographic position axis (TopoPC1) explained `r pct_var(pca_topo)`% of
topographic variance.

Median rarefied bacterial genus richness across plots was
`r med_div(sem_data_rich$Rich_16S)` genera (bacterial Shannon H':
`r round(median(sem_data_rich$Shan_16S * sd(rich_raw$Shan_16S, na.rm=TRUE) + mean(rich_raw$Shan_16S, na.rm=TRUE), na.rm=TRUE), 2)`),
and median fungal genus richness was `r med_div(sem_data_rich$Rich_ITS)` genera
(richness and Shannon H' averaged across 999 rarefaction draws).

#### Core SEM — environmental drivers of vegetation and soil development

The core path model provided `r fit_quality(sem_fit)` fit to the data
(`r chisq_str(sem_fit)`;
CFI = `r fi(sem_fit,"cfi")`;
RMSEA = `r fi(sem_fit,"rmsea")`;
SRMR = `r fi(sem_fit,"srmr")`).

Distance from the glacier terminus was a significant predictor of vegetation
colonisation (VegPC1: β = `r std_beta(sem_fit,"VegPC1","Dist_z")`,
*p* `r pval(sem_fit,"VegPC1","Dist_z")`), indicating that plots further from
the active glacier front had greater vegetation cover.
The topographic position axis (TopoPC1) also contributed to vegetation
development (β = `r std_beta(sem_fit,"VegPC1","TopoPC1")`,
*p* `r pval(sem_fit,"VegPC1","TopoPC1")`).
Together, these environmental predictors explained
R² = `r r2(sem_fit,"VegPC1")` of variation in VegPC1.

Vegetation colonisation was the strongest predictor of soil development
(SoilPC1: β = `r std_beta(sem_fit,"SoilPC1","VegPC1")`,
*p* `r pval(sem_fit,"SoilPC1","VegPC1")`), and the model explained
R² = `r r2(sem_fit,"SoilPC1")` of SoilPC1 variance.
The indirect effect of distance on soil development via vegetation was
β = `r def_est(sem_fit,"ind_dist")` (*p* `r def_p(sem_fit,"ind_dist")`),
and the total effect of distance on soil was
β = `r def_est(sem_fit,"tot_dist")` (*p* `r def_p(sem_fit,"tot_dist")`).

#### Microbial richness SEM — global-score reference

The parsimonious microbial richness model showed `r fit_quality(sem_rich)` fit
(`r chisq_str(sem_rich)`;
CFI = `r fi(sem_rich,"cfi")`;
RMSEA = `r fi(sem_rich,"rmsea")`).
Direct environmental paths to richness were omitted a priori, so distance and
topography affect microbial richness only through vegetation colonisation and
soil development.

Bacterial genus richness was significantly predicted by soil development
(β = `r std_beta(sem_rich,"Rich16S","SoilPC1")`,
*p* `r pval(sem_rich,"Rich16S","SoilPC1")`), but not by vegetation colonisation
(β = `r std_beta(sem_rich,"Rich16S","VegPC1")`,
*p* `r pval(sem_rich,"Rich16S","VegPC1")`).
The model explained R² = `r r2(sem_rich,"Rich16S")` of bacterial richness
variance.
In contrast, fungal genus richness was not significantly predicted by any
direct vegetation or soil variable in the model (both *p* > 0.05;
VegPC1: β = `r std_beta(sem_rich,"RichITS","VegPC1")`,
*p* `r pval(sem_rich,"RichITS","VegPC1")`;
SoilPC1: β = `r std_beta(sem_rich,"RichITS","SoilPC1")`,
*p* `r pval(sem_rich,"RichITS","SoilPC1")`),
with R² = `r r2(sem_rich,"RichITS")`.
The indirect effect of distance on bacterial richness through vegetation and
soil was β = `r def_est(sem_rich,"ind_dist_soil_16s")`
(*p* `r def_p(sem_rich,"ind_dist_soil_16s")`).

#### Final microbial richness SEM — partial PCA, trimmed paths

The final microbial richness SEM used the partial-PCA composite scores
(location centroid removed from VegPC1, SoilPC1, and TopoPC1) and then removed
direct pathways with *p* > `r trim_alpha` from the full Spec 1 richness model.
This retained `r nrow(partial_rich_direct_keep)` of
`r nrow(partial_rich_direct_full)` direct pathways.
The trimmed model showed `r fit_quality(sem_partial_rich_trim)` fit
(`r chisq_str(sem_partial_rich_trim)`;
CFI = `r fi(sem_partial_rich_trim,"cfi")`;
RMSEA = `r fi(sem_partial_rich_trim,"rmsea")`;
SRMR = `r fi(sem_partial_rich_trim,"srmr")`).
It explained R² = `r r2(sem_partial_rich_trim,"Rich16S")` of bacterial richness
and R² = `r r2(sem_partial_rich_trim,"RichITS")` of fungal richness.

#### Shannon diversity SEM

The parsimonious Shannon diversity model showed `r fit_quality(sem_shan)` fit
(`r chisq_str(sem_shan)`;
CFI = `r fi(sem_shan,"cfi")`;
RMSEA = `r fi(sem_shan,"rmsea")`).
As in the richness model, direct environmental paths to Shannon diversity were
excluded so that topographic and distance effects were evaluated as mediated
pathways through vegetation and soil.
Bacterial Shannon H' was predicted by soil development
(β = `r std_beta(sem_shan,"Shan16S","SoilPC1")`,
*p* `r pval(sem_shan,"Shan16S","SoilPC1")`),
consistent with the richness model.
Fungal Shannon H' was evaluated through direct vegetation and soil paths, plus
the bootstrapped indirect pathways from distance and TopoPC1.
The model explained R² = `r r2(sem_shan,"Shan16S")` and
R² = `r r2(sem_shan,"ShanITS")` of bacterial and fungal Shannon H' variance,
respectively.

#### Sensitivity analyses

Model specification had little effect on the core succession pathway.
In the partial PCA specification (location centroid removed from all composites),
the vegetation → soil relationship remained
(β = `r std_beta(sem_partial,"SoilPC1","VegPC1")`,
*p* `r pval(sem_partial,"SoilPC1","VegPC1")`),
and bacterial richness was again significantly predicted by soil development
(β = `r std_beta(sem_partial_rich,"Rich16S","SoilPC1")`,
*p* `r pval(sem_partial_rich,"Rich16S","SoilPC1")`).
When location was included as an explicit binary predictor (Spec 2), it
explained additional variance in both VegPC1
(β = `r std_beta(sem_loc,"VegPC1","Loc_bin")`,
*p* `r pval(sem_loc,"VegPC1","Loc_bin")`)
and SoilPC1
(β = `r std_beta(sem_loc,"SoilPC1","Loc_bin")`,
*p* `r pval(sem_loc,"SoilPC1","Loc_bin")`),
indicating that the two glacier systems differ in absolute levels of vegetation
and soil development beyond what is captured by distance and topographic
position alone.

## Methods text

### Main text (for manuscript)

Cover types (lichen, moss, biological soil crust, forbs, graminoids, bare soil,
stones), soil properties (organic matter, pH, total nitrogen, total phosphorus,
Na, Mg, K, Ca, coarse fraction >2 mm), and topographic attributes (elevation,
slope, TPI, aspect as sin/cos components, snow cover in 1976 as a binary
proxy for recent deglaciation) were each reduced to a single axis via principal
component analysis (PCA; `prcomp`, centered and scaled).
The first PC of cover variables (VegPC1), soil variables (SoilPC1), and
topographic variables (TopoPC1) served as composite indices of vegetation
colonisation, soil development, and topographic position, respectively.

Microbial genus richness and Shannon diversity (H') were computed separately
for bacteria (16S rRNA gene amplicons) and fungi (ITS amplicons).
Amplicon sequence variants were agglomerated to genus level (`phyloseq::tax_glom`)
and genus names standardised (`NetCoMi::renameTaxa`).
Counts from all microhabitat samples within each plot were pooled by summation,
then rarefied to the minimum pooled read depth observed across plots.
To minimise stochastic noise inherent in a single rarefaction draw, subsampling
was repeated 999 times and both richness (observed genera) and Shannon H' were
averaged across iterations (`vegan::rrarefy`, `vegan::diversity`).

Directional relationships among environmental gradients, vegetation colonisation,
soil development, and microbial diversity were examined using path analysis
(structural equation modelling, SEM) implemented in `lavaan` v0.6
[@Rosseel2012].
The hypothesised succession pathway was:
environmental predictors (Distance from glacier terminus; TopoPC1) →
vegetation colonisation (VegPC1) →
soil development (SoilPC1) →
microbial diversity (bacterial and fungal richness; bacterial and fungal Shannon H').
Direct environmental effects on soil were retained because distance and
topographic position may influence soil development independently of vegetation.
Direct environmental effects on microbial richness and Shannon diversity were
omitted in the primary microbial SEMs, making microbial responses terminal
outcomes of the vegetation-soil pathway.
All continuous predictors were z-scored prior to modelling. The final microbial
richness SEM used partial-PCA composite scores, in which between-location
centroid shifts were removed before extracting PC1 scores, and was trimmed by
removing direct pathways with *p* > 0.10 from the full partial-PCA richness SEM.
Path coefficients were standardised; standard errors and 95% confidence intervals
were obtained by parametric bootstrap (1,000 resamples, BCa intervals).
Global model fit was evaluated using the chi-squared statistic, Comparative Fit
Index (CFI ≥ 0.95), Root Mean Square Error of Approximation (RMSEA ≤ 0.08),
and Standardised Root Mean Square Residual (SRMR ≤ 0.08).

---

### Supplementary methods

#### S1. Principal component analyses

PCA was applied separately to the cover, soil, and topography variable blocks.
All variables were centred and scaled to unit variance before decomposition
(`prcomp(scale. = TRUE)`).
Snow cover in 1976 is a binary variable (0/1 indicating presence of glacier
ice on a 1976 Landsat image); it was treated as numeric for PCA, consistent
with its role as an ordinal terrain descriptor.
The proportion of total variance explained by PC1 and the variable loadings are
reported for each block (see biplots, above).

To assess whether the dominant PCA axes were consistent across the two glacier
systems (Nubra and Tsomoriri), we conducted two supplementary ordination
analyses: (i) **stratified PCAs** — independent PCAs within each location;
(ii) **partial PCAs** — `vegan::rda(mat ~ Condition(Location))`, which removes
the between-location centroid from the variable matrix before decomposition.
The proportion of total variance attributable to Location is reported as
R² from the partial RDA.
All three sets of PC1 scores (global, stratified, partial) were visualised as
biplots and compared. Global scores were retained for the core vegetation-soil
SEM, whereas the final microbial richness SEM used partial-PCA scores to focus
on within-location chronosequence structure.

#### S2. Rarefaction and diversity estimation

Read counts were pooled across microhabitat samples (Bulk Soil, Soil Crust,
Moss, Lichen, Plant) belonging to the same plot by summation of raw counts.
The minimum pooled read depth across all plots set the rarefaction target
(reported in the `sem-setup` chunk output).
Genus-level observed richness (number of genera with count > 0) and Shannon H'
were computed on each of 999 subsampled count matrices drawn without replacement
(`vegan::rrarefy`, seed 42), then averaged across iterations to give a
stable per-plot estimate.

#### S3. SEM model equations

The core model (4 nodes) estimated the following regression equations:

$$
\text{VegPC1} \sim \beta_{a1} \cdot \text{Dist}_z + \beta_{a2} \cdot \text{TopoPC1}
$$
$$
\text{SoilPC1} \sim \beta_b \cdot \text{VegPC1} + \beta_{c1} \cdot \text{Dist}_z + \beta_{c2} \cdot \text{TopoPC1}
$$

The extended model added microbial diversity as terminal outcomes:

$$
\text{Richness}_{16S} \sim \beta_{d1} \cdot \text{VegPC1} + \beta_{d2} \cdot \text{SoilPC1}
$$

with an analogous equation for ITS richness and for Shannon H'.
Direct paths from Distance or TopoPC1 to microbial outcomes were excluded in the
primary microbial SEMs to avoid a saturated specification and to match the
a priori chronosequence hypothesis that environmental effects on microbial
diversity are mediated through vegetation colonisation and soil development.
For the final microbial richness model, the full partial-PCA richness SEM was
further trimmed by removing direct pathways with *p* > 0.10, and the trimmed
model was compared with the full partial-PCA model using AIC, BIC, global fit
indices, and outcome R².
Residuals of the two marker-specific outcomes (bacteria and fungi) were allowed
to covary freely (`~~`), reflecting unmeasured shared environmental drivers.

Indirect effects were computed as products of labelled path coefficients
(e.g., Distance → Vegetation → Soil = $\hat\beta_{a1} \times \hat\beta_b$)
and bootstrapped alongside direct effects.

#### S4. Sensitivity analyses and model specification

Two additional model specifications were fitted to assess robustness to the
treatment of between-location variance:

- **Spec 1 (partial PCA)**: PC1 scores for VegPC1, SoilPC1, and TopoPC1 were
  extracted from partial RDAs conditioning on Location, removing between-location
  centroid shifts from all composites. Signs were aligned with the corresponding
  global PC1 (negated if Pearson r < 0).
- **Spec 2 (global PCA + Location)**: Global PC1 scores were retained and
  Location (binary dummy: Nubra = 1, Tsomoriri = 0) was added as an explicit
  exogenous predictor in all regression equations.

#### S5. Parsimony testing

```{r parsimony-test, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ── AIC comparison across all core SEM specifications ────────────────────────
aic_tbl <- tibble(
  Specification = c(
    "Global PCA (core)",
    "Partial PCA (core)",
    "Global PCA + Location (core)"
  ),
  AIC  = c(AIC(sem_fit), AIC(sem_partial), AIC(sem_loc)),
  BIC  = c(BIC(sem_fit), BIC(sem_partial), BIC(sem_loc))
) %>%
  mutate(
    delta_AIC = round(AIC - min(AIC), 2),
    delta_BIC = round(BIC - min(BIC), 2),
    AIC = round(AIC, 2),
    BIC = round(BIC, 2)
  ) %>%
  arrange(AIC)

aic_tbl %>%
  kable(caption = paste0(
    "AIC and BIC for the three core SEM specifications (4-node model). ",
    "delta = difference from best-fitting model. ",
    "Models within delta AIC < 2 are considered equivalent."
  )) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped","hover"), full_width = FALSE)

# ── Likelihood-ratio test: is Location a significant addition? ────────────────
# Compare global PCA (nested in global+Location via constraint a3=c3=0)
# Note: both must be fitted by ML (estimator="ML"), which they are.
cat("\nLRT: Global PCA vs Global PCA + Location\n")
lrt_loc <- lavTestLRT(sem_fit, sem_loc)
print(lrt_loc)

# ── Trimmed model: drop non-significant direct env paths from core SEM ────────
# A parsimonious model retains only paths with p < 0.10 in the full model.
sig_paths <- parameterEstimates(sem_fit) %>%
  filter(op == "~", pvalue < 0.10) %>%
  mutate(path_str = paste0(lhs, " ~ ", rhs))

cat("\nPaths retained in trimmed model (p < 0.10):\n")
print(sig_paths$path_str)

sem_model_trim <- paste(
  "VegPC1  ~",  paste(
    sig_paths %>% filter(lhs == "VegPC1")  %>% pull(rhs), collapse = " + "
  ),
  "\nSoilPC1 ~", paste(
    sig_paths %>% filter(lhs == "SoilPC1") %>% pull(rhs), collapse = " + "
  )
)

cat("\nTrimmed model:\n", sem_model_trim, "\n")

# Guard: only fit if both equations have at least one predictor
if (all(c("VegPC1", "SoilPC1") %in% sig_paths$lhs)) {
  sem_trim <- sem(
    sem_model_trim,
    data      = sem_data,
    estimator = "ML",
    se        = "bootstrap",
    bootstrap = 1000
  )

  cat("\nTrimmed model fit:\n")
  print(round(fitMeasures(sem_trim, c("chisq","df","pvalue","cfi","rmsea","srmr")), 3))

  cat("\nLRT: Full core SEM vs trimmed model\n")
  # Trimmed is nested within full if only paths are removed (no new constraints)
  tryCatch(
    print(lavTestLRT(sem_trim, sem_fit)),
    error = function(e) cat("LRT not applicable (models not nested):", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
  )

  cat("\nAIC comparison (full vs trimmed):\n")
  print(tibble(
    Model = c("Full (core)", "Trimmed"),
    AIC   = round(c(AIC(sem_fit), AIC(sem_trim)), 2),
    BIC   = round(c(BIC(sem_fit), BIC(sem_trim)), 2)
  ))
} else {
  cat("One or both SoilPC1/VegPC1 equations have no retained predictors — trimmed model skipped.\n")
}
```
